tweets.text:
If you still have doubts about whether you should build your personal brand, here’s the answer:

You should.
Especially if you run a B2B business.

Edelman ran a great study based on input from 1,934 management-level LinkedIn members – and many of them explicitly signal that thought leadership strongly impacts their decisions.

Some facts:

• 95% of hidden buyers say strong thought leadership makes them more open to outreach
• 73% of US hidden B2B buyers judge the calibre of a company’s thinking by its thought leadership
• 64% of hidden buyers trust thought leadership more than product sheets to judge vendor capability

So yeah, a founder persona is one of the best investments you can make for your business – especially if you’re selling to other companies.

Think about it ;)

A big reason @base has moved ahead of @BNBCHAIN and @solana in DeFi TVL is how easily you can access onchain lending.

DeFi TVL per @DefiLlama:

→ Base: $5.77B
→ BNB Chain: $5.05B
→ Solana: $5.02B

Through @coinbase, you can borrow $USDC against your assets without leaving the app, while @Morpho handles the lending on Base.

That integration held ~$3.4B in collateral and $1.7B+ in active loans.

So you're getting onchain lending through an app you already know, which helps explain the scale Base has reached.

Kudos to the Base team for this achievement.

fun! listing a few places below, also recommend checking our airbnb experiences and finding some random things on there - we did chopstick making, leatherworks, tea ceremony, sushi making, flower arranging, etc, just a bunch of things we'd never experience elsewhere and they were all pretty much awesome

Osaka

Super cool little retro gaming bar: https://t.co/eUYEtyjZjZ

S-tier escape room, we've done like 50 of them in the world and this is one of the best: https://t.co/5LbxwIjFNO

This is just one of those wtf things that is so-Japan, it's like a 7 story sex shop: https://t.co/Id3uwdaOfI

I dunno how into coffee you are but if you're a big coffee nerd, you'll probably like this cafe: https://t.co/ug4W5ZBHVq

Tokyo

Really cool authentic restaurant, lovely people running it. Cash only, you have to take off your shoes when you get in. Not overly expensive (if you go for dinner they let you share the dinner set too if you're not that hungry): https://t.co/Ftakpd1MJh

If you like retro gaming, this place is awesome - lots of nostalgia and gaming things from ages ago, although mostly in japanese. Worth checking out if you're in the area though (and akihabara is worth visiting, the arcades are crazy and fun): https://t.co/DJAMIU8B6M

I think the best case is to make the "monitor" as un-agentic as possible.

We don't mind being "monitored" by various random tiny insects we don't even notice, even guard dogs are fine, but we really do mind if it's a globally connected networked system. And the intermediate case, human security guards with no recording equipment, we mind only a medium amount.

The best idea I've come up with so far is to make these monitoring devices out of open-source verifiable hardware that has etched on it an open-weight LLM that classifies for a limited number of activities (basically, just violence; sorry, no scanning for jaywalking or not wearing a mask or drugs or unauthorized manufacturing or illegal immigrants, really just violence) and only records and forwards if that's what it sees. The device has no storage, no ability to load new algorithms, this is all it does.

Also, a hash of every recording is published onchain (and a device can't record the next one until it sees confirmation of the previous one) so we can all count how much recording is done.

Finally, everyone has a legal right to take any such device they see and grab it and dissassemble and verify the hardware themselves. Explicitly fund university clubs, hacker groups, etc to regularly do this.

David Friedberg: Was Jensen Taken Out So the Deep State Could Control AI?

@friedberg:

“I do worry that there is legislation coming our way with the new Congress that is going to say, ‘Every AI chip and every computer and every data center has a switch and has a connection back to some central system.’ And that central system will be a state system.

And we are fundamentally looking at an Orwellian state explosion if this sort of thing happens.

And my guess is that people know Jensen's philosophy.

Jensen has talked a lot about AI being for the benefit of all of humanity, regardless of your country, regardless of your standing, regardless of your wealth.

He was anti-oligopoly, he was the opposite of the oligarchy.

And the central state, the totalitarian state, represents everything that I believe Jensen was against.

And because of that, I think he had to be taken out if ultimately the goal is to have the totalitarian state use this technology as a tool.”

I went to the Apple Store to try the iPhone Duo, and I realized: I don't want more screen space. I don't want to do more things in parallel on my phone or have two apps open instead of one. I want technology to disappear. I want an AI to pre-draft my emails and SMS messages, manage my calendar conflicts, and tell me what's up.

The true magic is to do less. To delegate more to technology. Ultimately, I don't even want to type anything. I just want to give some basic voice instructions.

True magic is when you make technology disappear. It's not 2 screens it's 0.
